аблакат.note: Dialectal/nonstandard spelling of адвокат, used in the folk saying 'аблакат – нанятая совесть' (a hired conscience).

автодафе.note: From Portuguese auto da fé, an Inquisition ceremony where heretics were sentenced and burned; used in the Grand Inquisitor legend.

адвокатишка.note: Pejorative diminutive of адвокат; text has genitive plural адвокатишек.

ажно.note: Colloquial/dialectal variant of аж (even, so that).

ажный.note: Wrong headword; the form is ажно, a colloquial variant of аж.

ай-люли.note: Colloquial refrain from folk songs, here used mockingly for 'and so on, nonsense'.

акриды.note: Church Slavonic/biblical word (акрида); the food of John the Baptist in the wilderness.

акриды-то.note: Form of акриды with the particle -то; see акрида (locust, biblical food of hermits).

ананасный.note: Adjective from ананас; 'ананасный компот' means pineapple compote.

ангел-барышня.note: Ironic/effusive form of address used by Grushenka toward Katerina Ivanovna.

антидорцу.note: Dative of антидор/антидорец; the blessed bread distributed after liturgy. Here it means a mere crumb of food.

аплодисмент.note: Singular form of аплодисменты, which is normally plural; here a single burst of applause.

апокрифический.note: Refers to non-canonical religious texts; here the apocryphal Gospels.

артистическа.note: Misspelled headword; the correct form is артистически, from артистический.

артистически.note: Used here ironically of human cruelty.

архиподлец.note: Formed with the intensifying prefix архи-; the text has it in the nominative singular.

архитриклиновить.note: Wrong headword; the form архитриклинови is the Church Slavonic dative of архитриклин (master of the feast), from the wedding at Cana quote.

архитриклиновь.note: Wrong headword; the correct lemma is архитриклин. Church Slavonic dative архитриклинови, from the Gospel of John (Cana).

архиультрамонтанство.note: Coined with архи- from ультрамонтанство (ultramontanism, extreme support for papal authority).

аршинный.note: From аршин, an old measure of about 71 cm; 'аршинными шагами' means with long, striding steps.

бабусенька.note: Affectionate diminutive of бабуся/бабушка; here fondly applied to Russia.

байроновский.note: From Byron, the English poet, whose heroes are proud, brooding rebels.

бакалейный.note: Used in 'бакалейный магазин', a grocery shop selling dry goods.

бальзамчик.note: Diminutive of бальзам; here a medicinal or herbal liqueur.

банкер.note: The bank-holder in a gambling game; here in the mouth of the Poles' card scene.

бардзо.note: Polish (bardzo); used in the speech of the Polish characters.

бардзый.note: Wrong headword; the form is Polish bardzo (very), spoken by the Polish characters.

бариновый.note: Possessive adjective from барин, colloquial; here 'the master's trust'.

барчонок.note: Diminutive of барин (gentleman), a young son of the gentry; often slightly derogatory.

барынька.note: Diminutive of барыня (lady, mistress); tone varies from fondness to mild contempt.

баснословие.note: Dated bookish word for myths and fables.

баш.note: From Turkic baş (head); 'баш на баш' is a colloquial idiom meaning an even exchange.

бе.note: Church Slavonic imperfect of быти ('to be'), as in Gospel quotations like 'и бе мати Иисусова ту'.

беглянка.note: Feminine of беглец; here a woman who ran away from home.

безбожество.note: Rare/dated; text has dative безбожеству ('to his godlessness').

безвинный-с.note: безвинны-с: the servile particle -с (from сударь) is added, as Smerdyakov speaks; base word безвинный

безвременный.note: in the Fyodor Pavlovich quote, безвременном is used loosely (roughly 'decrepit, out of time'); a stretched, unusual usage

безответность.note: here: not answering back, passive meekness

безотлучный.note: text form безотлучно is an adverb: 'without leaving, constantly at one's side'

безотчетность.note: безотчетность is the ё-less spelling; describes feelings one cannot account for

безудерж.note: variant of безудержность; in the phrase 'karamazovian безудерж' = reckless lack of restraint

безудержать.note: the analyzer's headword is wrong; безудержу is the genitive of the noun безудерж ('unrestraint, impetuosity')

безурядица.note: dated/literary; here: the disorder of Russia

безыскусственный.note: text form безыскусствен is the short form; безыскусственно is the adverb

g: idle landowner who avoids manual labor
белоручек-помещик.note: the correct lemma is белоручка (person who avoids manual work) + помещик (landowner); plural genitive белоручек-помещиков

g: idle landowner who avoids manual labor
белоручка-помещик.note: белоручка = person who shuns manual labor, a dandy/idler; помещик = landowner; genitive plural форма белоручек-помещиков

бельишечко.note: affectionate double diminutive of бельё (linen, underwear); dialect/folk speech

беснование.note: here: the possessed fits of the klikushi (hysterical women believed possessed)

бесова.note: possessive adjective from бес (demon), feminine/genitive form used in folk speech; бесова сына = 'devil's son'

бесцензурность.note: unusual coinage; here: speaking without any propriety or restraint

бечева.note: used for hauling barges (бечевою тянуть = to tow by rope, by burlak)

бечевой.note: headword is wrong; the form бечевою is the instrumental of бечева (towline, tow rope), used to tow barges

бечевочка.note: diminutive of бечёвка (string); text spelling бечевочки without ё

биллиардный.note: old spelling of бильярдный; биллиардной is used as a noun = billiard room

биющий-то.note: Dialectal/archaic participle of бить ('биющих' = бьющих), a quoted phrase 'бьющих на чувствительность' = playing for sympathy. Lemma is odd; correct lemma is бьющий.

благовестить.note: Church Slavonic-flavored; originally 'to announce good news'.

благовестный.note: 'Благовестный звон' = the bell ringing calling to service; derived from благовест.

g: to be in a placid, good-humored mood
благодушествовать.note: Somewhat bookish; here of a drunkard-in-the-making being genially contented.

благонравный.note: Form 'благонравно' is the adverb; used ironically here.

благословишисить.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong. Text has 'благословишися' = Church Slavonic imperative/subjunctive form of благословитися ('be blessed'); part of a ritual formula 'Благословляя да благословишися'.

благочиние.note: Also a church term (supervision of parishes), but here means propriety, order.

блажной-с.note: Form 'блажные-с' = plural of блажной with servile particle -с (Smerdyakov's speech style).

блудилище.note: Archaic/bookish word for a house of ill repute.

бо.note: Church Slavonic conjunction (as in Bible quotations).

богадельный.note: From богадельня (almshouse); 'дом богадельный' = a home like an almshouse.

боговидица.note: Church Slavonic-style epithet, here of St. Mary of Egypt; feminine of боговидец.

богомолье.note: Trip to holy places to pray.

богомольный.note: Also used of pilgrims; 'богомольные старушки' = devout old women.

богопочтение.note: Archaic/poetic; genitive-like form 'богопочтенья' appears in a quoted verse.

g: to put on a brave, cheerful face

бозить.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong: 'бози' is Church Slavonic plural of 'бог' (gods), from the biblical 'яко бози' = 'like gods'.

бозь.note: Wrong lemma: 'бози' is Church Slavonic nominative plural of бог; from Genesis 'яко бози' ('as gods').

болезние.note: Archaic/wrong lemma: 'болезнию' = instrumental of болезнь; 'за болезнию' = on account of illness (old form of the case ending).

болоночко.note: Wrong lemma: correct is болоночка (feminine), a diminutive of болонка (lapdog).

борать.note: Wrong lemma: 'борет' is colloquial/dialectal 3rd person of бороть/бороться... correct form is бороть ('to fight'); 'себя борет' = fights herself, restrains herself.

бороть.note: Older/colloquial form of побороть/одолевать; 'себя борет' = struggles with herself.

бременить.note: Archaic; 'не бременить землю' = not to burden the earth (with one's existence).

брыкливость.note: From брыкливый (prone to kick/buck); here his refractory conduct.

бульонщик.note: Contemptuous nickname/insult, meaning one who makes broth (e.g. cook); appears as Grigory's insult to Smerdyakov.

бухнуться.note: Colloquial; 'бухнуться в ноги' = fall at someone's feet.

быдто.note: Dialectal/colloquial form of 'будто'; here used as an ironic 'as if you don't know'.

быдтый.note: Wrong headword; the text form is just the colloquial particle 'быдто' (= будто).

бысть.note: Church Slavonic aorist of быти (to be); archaic. Not a modern Russian word.

вакация.note: Dated word from Latin 'vacatio'; used of school/university holidays (usually plural 'вакации').

валаамов.note: Possessive adjective of Валаам (Balaam); 'валаамова ослица' is Balaam's ass, the talking donkey of the Bible (Numbers 22).

ввернуть.note: Here: to interject a remark into conversation. Forms ввернул/ввернуто are past tense/participle.

ввертывать.note: Imperfective of ввернуть; here: inserting the banknotes into the envelope.

вдовица.note: Archaic/literary or Church Slavonic-flavored word for вдова.

вдовый.note: Dated; said of a man whose wife has died (widower).

велено.note: Impersonal passive of велеть (to order): 'it was ordered that'.

великодушничать.note: Colloquial, often ironic: to put on generosity/magnanimity toward someone.

великомученический.note: From великомученик (great martyr); here: a cross/burden of martyr-like suffering.

велице.note: Church Slavonic adverb; here the form 'велицем' belongs to велий (great), as in 'великая четверток'. Archaic.

велицый.note: Church Slavonic form (= великий); 'о велицем четвертке' refers to Great (Holy) Thursday. Archaic.

вервие.note: Church Slavonic/archaic; here the rope belt of a monk's cassock.

верзиться.note: Dialectal/colloquial spelling; 'верзись вниз' = 'throw yourself down' (from the Temptation of Christ). Likely a form of 'ввергнуться/ввергаться' or 'верзиться' in older usage.

верниссимо.note: Jocular Italianate superlative of 'верно' (correct), used playfully.

версточка.note: Diminutive of верста (verst, about 1.07 km); 'версточек' is genitive plural, used to make the distance seem short.

верстушка.note: Affectionate diminutive of верста (verst); used to minimize the distance.

верстушко.note: Wrong headword; the text form 'верстушка' is a diminutive of верста (verst).

веруесать.note: Wrong headword; 'веруеши' is Church Slavonic 2nd person singular of веровати ('како веруеши' = how do you believe). Archaic.

взвар.note: Old Russian dish: a drink/stewed fruit boiled with honey, common in monastic fare.

взлезть.note: Colloquial; here: to climb onto the cart.

взмоститься.note: Colloquial/dated; 'взмостясь' is the gerund, 'having climbed up onto something'.

взрасти.note: Archaic/literary variant of взрасти/возрасти; 'взросшая' is a participle 'brought up'.

взрезать.note: Here in the sense of tearing open/cutting into the earth's breast; 'взрезаю' is 1st person singular.

взыск.note: Dated noun from взыскать; 'большого взыску не будет' = there won't be a heavy penalty.

взямшить.note: Wrong headword; 'взямши' is Smerdyakov's uneducated gerund of взять ('having taken/supposing'), used as a filler. Nonstandard.

видзел.note: Polish 'widział' (in Russian transliteration), from widzieć 'to see'; spoken by the Polish characters.

видзен.note: Polish-flavored fragment (Polish 'widzę'/'widzieć'); in a broken Polish phrase meaning roughly 'I see (you're) unfriendly and I am gloomy'.

видзение.note: Polish 'widzenie'; appears only in 'до видзенья' = Polish 'do widzenia', goodbye.

видзений.note: Wrong headword; 'до видзенья' is Polish 'do widzenia' (goodbye).

видзеть.note: Polish 'widzieć' (to see) in Russian transliteration; the form 'видзел' is Polish 'widział' (saw).

виляние.note: Verbal noun of вилять; here figuratively, dodging/equivocating before the court.

височек.note: Diminutive of висок (temple); 'височки' = little locks of hair combed forward at the temples.

вкатить.note: Here: to roll/drive a bullet into the gun barrel.

владетельный.note: archaic; typically of princes ('владетельный князь'); no context given

властие.note: Church Slavonic/archaic form of власть; here instrumental 'властию'

вмешивать.note: imperfective of вмешать; here 'bring in (a judgment by merit)'

внаймы.note: variant of внаём; отдаваться внаймы = be offered for rent

внеправда.note: Dostoevsky's nonstandard formation; 'внеправду' = insincerely, not in truth

внушаться.note: here 'внушайтесь' = let yourselves be swayed; 'внушаясь' = being influenced by

водворяться.note: here of the institution of eldership taking hold in monasteries

водевильчик.note: diminutive of водевиль; figuratively light-hearted antics

водонос.note: Church Slavonic (John 2:7, wedding at Cana); 'водоносы' = water jars

возгордиться.note: Church Slavonic flavor; 'возгордясь' is the gerund

возгривый.note: dialectal/archaic; from гривa; here spoken by a peasant describing a man

возжигать.note: Church Slavonic; used of lighting lamps (лампады)

возмериться.note: from the biblical 'какою мерою мерите, возмерится вам'

возненавидиш.note: Church Slavonic 2nd sg. form 'возненавидиши'; here in 'ниже возненавидиши' = nor hate; modern возненавидишь

вознепщеваха.note: Church Slavonic aorist/imperfect (here spelled вознепщеваху); mocking quotation of church language; from вознепщевати 'to suppose'

возношение.note: Church Slavonic flavor; here 'without exalting oneself over them'

возроптать.note: biblical/literary; forms возропщет, возропщешь are future

вольнопрактикующий.note: dated; of a doctor or dentist practicing privately; here used as a noun

g: to take it into one's head
вообразиться.note: impersonal with dative: мне вообразилось = it seemed to me

вор-то-с.note: вор + emphatic -то + servile particle -с (from сударь); here genitive 'вора-то-с'

вороненький.note: diminutive of вороной; 'вороненькую лошадку' = little black horse

воспарять.note: imperfective of воспарить; literary, from a quoted line

воспламеняться.note: Here figurative: flare up with anger.

восприемница.note: Church term, archaic; feminine of восприемник.

воссиять.note: Elevated/Church Slavonic style; second sense: truth shines forth (comes to light).

восст.note: Wrong headword; the form восста is Church Slavonic aorist of воста́ти (воскреснуть), 'arose', from the Gospel phrase 'and the girl arose'.

восстани.note: Church Slavonic imperative of восстати; Gospel-style command.

восстый.note: Wrong headword; восста is Church Slavonic aorist of воста́ти, 'arose' (from 'and the girl arose').

востордить.note: Wrong headword; восторжен is short form of восторженный.

восторжный.note: Short form восторжен; standard form is восторженный.

востро.note: Colloquial; in idiom держать ухо востро: keep one's wits about one, be on guard.

вострый.note: Archaic/dialectal form of острый; text has adverb востро in the idiom держать ухо востро.

восхостить.note: Church Slavonic; correct lemma is восхотеть; восхощу is 1st person singular future ('I shall wish').

восчувствовать.note: Archaic/bookish, with a slightly ironic tone here; 'not feel contempt for me'.

восьмиконечный.note: Orthodox term: eight-pointed cross, embroidered on the monastic schema/cowl.

вправить.note: Here: to put the icon on him, tucking it in under the collar.

вправлять.note: Imperfective of вправить; here: tuck her braid back / fasten the icon.

впросак.note: Idiom попасть впросак: to get into an embarrassing mess, to be caught out.

впрягать.note: Впрягай is imperative; впрягали is past plural.

врачество.note: Church Slavonic/archaic; in the elder's quoted text.

врыть.note: Врытый is past passive participle: dug into the ground.

вседержитель.note: Church Slavonic epithet of God, here used loosely; 'Бог вседержитель' = God Almighty.

всее.note: Nonstandard spelling of всю (accusative of вся); here used with 'себя', a colloquial/dialectal emphatic form.

всемилостивый.note: Elevated/religious; declined form всемилостивой, used of God or the Virgin.

вскачь.note: Often with гнать/пустить: drive at a gallop.

всклочить.note: Colloquial; всклочены is short passive participle: (hair) tousled.

вскоца.note: Wrong headword; вскоцу is a dialectal/childish form of вскочу ('I will jump up'), with the ц-for-ч pronunciation (цоканье), in the peasant girl's saying 'захоцу — вскоцу'.

вскрикивание.note: Noun from вскрикивать; plural instrumental here.

вспалый.note: Wrong headword; вспало is neuter past of вспасть (на ум): 'it came into his head'.

вспать.note: Archaic/colloquial; used only in вспасть на ум ('to come to one's mind').

вспомянуть.note: Archaic/church-style form of вспомнить; used for praying for someone by name.

вспорхнуться.note: Nonstandard reflexive form of вспорхнуть (to take flight); here 'she fluttered up all excited'.

вспрыгнуть.note: Things on the table 'jumped up' from the blow.

вспрыснуть.note: Imperative Вспрысни; here sprinkle him with water sprayed from the mouth (folk remedy for fainting).

встыд.note: Polish-style form (Polish wstyd); appears in Polish-influenced speech of the Polish officer; the analyzer's headword is questionable.

встыда.note: Wrong headword; the text has 'без встыду', pseudo-Polish for 'shamelessly, without shame' (Polish wstyd).

втюриться.note: Colloquial; usually 'to fall head over heels in love', here 'to get involved in a foolish affair'.

вывертывание.note: Verbal noun from выворачивать/вывёртывать; here describes Maximov's dance of splaying his feet outward.

выдавиться.note: Blood 'squeezed out' from under the nail; a sad smile 'appeared' on his lips (figurative).

выделанно.note: Adverb of выделанный in the sense of 'contrived, put-on'.

выделанный.note: The form in text is the adverb выделанно (affectedly, in a contrived way).

выздоровить.note: Nonstandard/colloquial form of выздороветь; here 'I will get well'.

выказываться.note: Reflexive/passive of выказывать; 'began to show and reveal itself'.

g: to cry out (as a possessed woman)
выкликать.note: Folk term: 'кликуша' is a hysterical woman who shrieks as if possessed; 'кликушей выкликать' = to start shrieking like one.

выколачивать.note: Two uses: 'выколачивать деньгу' = squeeze out money; 'руду выколачивать' = hammer out ore.

выкушать.note: Polite/humorous variant of выпить/съесть (from кушать); here he drank just one small glass of punch.

вымаливание.note: Verbal noun from вымаливать (to obtain by begging).

вымбыть.note: Wrong headword; the text has the infinitive выместь (to sweep out), an old form of вымести.

выместь.note: Archaic/colloquial infinitive of вымести; 'have the square swept'.

вымученно.note: Adverb of вымученный; here used predicatively: it would come out forced.

вымученный.note: Text form вымученно is the adverb/short form (forced, strained).

вымучить.note: Text form вымученного is the participle: 'forced, strained (rapture)'.

выпучиться.note: Colloquial; 'выпучившийся взгляд' = a fixed, bulging-eyed stare.

выпытать.note: Perfective; 'I couldn't get anything out of her'.

вырезание.note: Verbal noun from вырезать; here cutting babies out of the mother's womb.

выс-сечь.note: Spelling of высечь with drawn-out 'с' to show the doctor's angry hissing; 'must be flogged!'

выскрести.note: Colloquial; 'will scrape out the last scrapings'.

выслужиться.note: Here 'выслужился' means he rose in rank again; 'выслужившийся' describes a man risen from the ranks.

выслушание.note: Bureaucratic-style verbal noun from выслушать; 'перейдем к выслушанию' = let us proceed to hearing.

высоконравственный.note: Formal, somewhat ironic compound used by the lawyer.

высокооткроветь.note: Wrong headword; the text word is the adjective высокооткровенный (extremely frank).

высокопреподобие.note: Honorific for an abbot: 'ваше высокопреподобие'; 'его высокопреподобие' refers to him in the third person.

высокоталантливый.note: Used with ironic/formal flourish in the trial speeches.

высунить.note: Form высуня is a gerund of высунуть (colloquial spelling); 'высуня язык' = with tongue hanging out.

выцарапать.note: 'глаза выцарапать' = to scratch someone's eyes out.

g: to let out drop by drop
выцеживать.note: Here figurative: uttering words one at a time, reluctantly.

вычесывать.note: Form вычесывал is imperfective past; here 'combed lice out of'.

вьельфилька.note: Nonstandard rendering of French 'vieille fille'; jocular/colloquial.

вящший.note: Archaic Church Slavonic; form вящше is comparative used adverbially: 'вящше же ничто же' = nothing more.

гадательный.note: Here: uncertain, unfathomable (things beyond human strength).

гадливый.note: Adverb гадливо = with disgust; гадливое презрение = disdainful loathing.

галдарея.note: Dialect/colloquial form of галерея; here as the inn's gallery.

галдареять.note: Wrong headword: галдарею is the accusative of noun галдарея (gallery, dialectal form of галерея).

гамлетовский.note: From Shakespeare's Hamlet; 'гамлетовские вопросы' = questions about what comes after death.

гантированный.note: From obsolete гантировать (from French gant, glove).

гантировать.note: Obsolete; from French gant. Form гантированную is a past passive participle: gloved.

гарнитуровый.note: Old word for a cheap, coarse dress fabric (garniture); here a jeer at Alyosha's trousers.

гвоздочка.note: Diminutive of гвоздь; the analyzer's headword is off, the form гвоздочке is prepositional singular of гвоздочек.

гвоздочко.note: Wrong headword; correct lemma is гвоздочек (diminutive of гвоздь).

геморроидальный.note: Used of a sickly, yellowish complexion.

генеральша-старуха.note: Compound of генеральша (general's wife) and старуха (old woman); genitive form генеральши-старухи.

генеральши-старуха.note: Wrong headword; correct lemma is генеральша-старуха (genitive генеральши-старухи).

геометр.note: Here plural геометры; refers to mathematicians/geometers (cf. non-Euclidean geometry).

гернгутер.note: Member of the Moravian Church (Herrnhut, German); the text itself glosses it as 'моравский брат'.

гернгутереть.note: Wrong headword; the form гернгутер is the noun (Herrnhuter, Moravian Brother).

гешефт.note: From German Geschäft; colloquial/slangy, often with a disparaging tone.

гл.note: Abbreviation of глава (chapter), as in a Bible reference.

глаголати.note: Church Slavonic infinitive of глаголать; archaic, in a quoted liturgical/biblical text.

глаголать.note: Archaic/Church Slavonic; глаголет = speaks, says; глагола = said.

глупенький.note: Diminutive of глупый; often affectionate or condescending.

гноиться.note: Form гноящийся is a present active participle: festering, oozing pus.

гнусненький.note: Diminutive of гнусный, used with contemptuous irony.

голенький.note: Diminutive of голый; here bare little hands of a child.

головорезный.note: Colloquial; derived from головорез (cutthroat, daredevil). Here: reckless, life-risking pranks.

голосочек.note: Diminutive of голос (voice); affectionate, in the instrumental case (голосочком).

голоштанник-с.note: Colloquial, contemptuous (lit. one without trousers). The -с is the servile particle from сударь, used by Smerdyakov.

голубина.note: Church Slavonic form: 'в виде голубине' = in the form of a dove. Correct lemma is голубиный; the phrase is a stylised liturgical/biblical echo.

голубиный.note: Голубиная душа = a gentle, innocent soul (affectionate address).

голыш.note: Colloquial; literally a naked one, also a bare pebble. Here: a pauper with nothing.

гомеопатический-то.note: Form Гомеопатические-то with emphatic particle -то. Here: tiny, homeopathic doses.

горбатенький-то.note: Diminutive of горбатый (hunchbacked) with emphatic particle -то; affectionate.

гордое-прегордый.note: Wrong headword; the text has гордое-прегордое, neuter of гордый-прегордый, an intensifying folk-style repetition with пре-.

гордый-прегордый.note: Intensifying doubling with the prefix пре-; here neuter form гордое-прегордое, modifying сердечко.

горестие.note: Archaic, Church Slavonic form of горесть; горестию is the instrumental (with grief).

горлан.note: Colloquial; someone who shouts loudly; plural горланы.

горошинка.note: Diminutive of горошина (a pea). 'Сделать из горошинки гору' is like making a mountain out of a molehill.

горьчайший.note: Superlative of горький; the neuter form горьчайшее appears in the text.

горячий-горячий.note: Wrong headword; the text has the adverb горячо-горячо, a doubled adverb meaning very warmly/passionately.

горячо-горячий.note: Wrong headword; the text has the adverb горячо-горячо, a repetition for emphasis.

горячо-горячо.note: Doubling of горячо for emphasis, typical of emotional speech.

господчик.note: Diminutive of господин, here slightly ironic or dismissive.

готув.note: Polish gotów (ready) in Polish speech: 'Естем готув' = 'jestem gotów' = I am ready. Foreign word.

готуть.note: Wrong headword; the text is Polish gotów (ready), from 'Естем готув' = 'jestem gotów' = I am ready.

гощение.note: Archaic/dated; the act of being a guest (from гостить); genitive гощения.

гравюрный.note: Related to гравюра (engraving); 'гравюрные изображения' are engraved pictures.

гражданственник.note: Rare; someone who champions civic/social ideals (from гражданственность).

грешничка.note: Affectionate diminutive of грешница, plural форма грешнички; here in a folk-religious tone.

грозд.note: Archaic/poetic form of гроздь; plural грозды. From Schiller's Ode to Joy in Russian translation.

грозда.note: Wrong headword; text has plural грозды of archaic грозд/гроздь (a cluster of grapes).

гроздие.note: Archaic/poetic collective; genitive Гроздий in the poetic verse quoted.

грошик.note: Diminutive of грош (a small old copper coin of little value); plural грошики.

грязненький.note: Diminutive of грязный; here used both literally (a grubby scrap) and figuratively (sordid doubts).

грязноватый.note: Form грязновато used predicatively; -оват- gives the sense of 'rather'.

губенка-то.note: Colloquial, with emphatic particle -то; губенки is the plural of the diminutive губёнка (from губа, lip), used with pity.

губительница.note: Feminine of губитель; instrumental case губительницей.

гуртовщик.note: One who drives a herd (гурт) of livestock to market.

гусынька.note: Affectionate diminutive of гусыня (goose); here from a children's rhyme.

дав.note: Wrong headword; the text has the colloquial adverb даве (earlier, a while ago), from давеча.

давленый.note: Participial adjective from давить; 'как паук давленый' = like a squashed spider.

дантовский.note: Relating to Dante; here Dante-like boldness of imagining torments.

даровитость.note: Abstract noun from даровитый; spoken ironically by Rakitin.

даровой.note: Neuter form даровое; here 'a free show' (даровое представление).

два-три.note: Fixed hyphenated approximate quantity; feminine form две-три with feminine nouns.

двесец.note: Wrong headword: the form двесьце is Polish-flavored speech (Polish dwieście), spoken by the Polish characters.

двоиться.note: Here of the Milky Way looking indistinct/doubled.

двухаршинный.note: An arshin is about 71 cm; here of a dress train.

девчоночка.note: Diminutive of девчонка; colloquial, here a girl of loose morals.

делишек.note: Wrong headword: the form делишку is accusative singular of делишко, a diminutive of дело (business, matter), often slightly shady.

делишки.note: Plural of делишко, a diminutive of дело; slightly pejorative, colloquial.

деньги‑то‑с.note: деньги + emphatic particle то + servile particle -с (short for сударь, sir).

дерзновенный.note: Elevated/Church Slavonic style; the forms in text are short forms and adverb/comparative.

деспотическа.note: Wrong headword; the correct one is деспотически.

десятирублевый.note: Here used as a noun: a ten-ruble note.

десятитысячный.note: Here 'на десятитысячную' means 'to the extent of one ten-thousandth'.

детей-младенец.note: Wrong headword: the text has детей-младенцев, i.e. two infant children (genitive plural).

детушки.note: Plural of детушка; folk/endearing diminutive of дети, used in peasant speech.

диаволов.note: Archaic possessive adjective from диавол; correct form here is диаволово (neuter).

диаволово.note: Neuter possessive of archaic диавол (devil): 'the devil's third temptation'.

диаволовый.note: Wrong headword; the form is possessive диаволов, -а, -о from archaic диавол.

дить.note: Wrong headword: жено is the vocative of жена (woman/wife), Church Slavonic style address, as in Jesus's words 'жено'.

дитять.note: Wrong headword; the form дитятю is accusative of дитятя, a folk/dialect variant of дитя.

дитятя.note: Colloquial/folk form of дитя; here accusative дитятю, spoken by a peasant woman.

длинно-длинный.note: Wrong headword; the form is the adverb reduplication длинно-длинно, 'at very great length'.

длинноватый.note: Here short plural: длинноваты, said of trousers.

длинную-длинный.note: Wrong headword; the text has the reduplicated accusative длинную-длинную улицу, 'a very, very long street'.

длинный-длинный.note: Reduplication for emphasis; adverbial длинно-длинно and accusative длинную-длинную occur in text.

довременный.note: Rare/bookish; the adverb довременно means 'prior to time, eternally'.

догадамнуться.note: Wrong headword; the form догадамшись is Smerdyakov's comic, nonstandard participle of догадаться (to guess, realize), with an illiterate-servant ending.

догадамшиться.note: Wrong headword; догадамшись is a deliberately illiterate/comic form of the gerund of догадаться.

додача.note: Rare/colloquial; from доддавать/додать (to add what is lacking).

дожидать.note: Dialectal/colloquial; standard form is дожидаться (+ genitive). Here 'дожидал их' means 'was waiting for them'.

дознать.note: Rare; дознано is the neuter short passive participle, 'it has been established'. Related to дознание (inquiry).

доказаться.note: Reflexive/passive of доказать; used here half-jokingly by the investigator after 'окажется'.

докладываться.note: Here: to inform Smerdyakov beforehand, to consult him. Imperfective reflexive of доложиться.

докторша.note: Colloquial feminine of доктор, meaning the wife of a doctor (not a female doctor).

долголетний.note: Here in the feminine genitive: 'after a long separation of many years'.

долечить.note: Perfective; долечит is 3rd person future, 'will finish treating'.

доложиться.note: Reflexive of доложить; 'доложитесь' = have yourself announced/report your arrival.

долюбить.note: Perfective formed with до- ('to the end'); poetic use, 'let me finish loving'.

донага.note: Used with раздеть: to strip completely naked.

донушка.note: Diminutive of дно (bottom); the text's донушке is prepositional case, 'on the very bottom'.

донушко.note: Diminutive of дно; the correct nominative is донышко/донушко, here in the prepositional case.

g: of the time before Peter the Great
допетровский.note: Refers to Old Russia before Peter I's reforms; 'допетровская старина' = pre-Petrine antiquity.

доплатить.note: Here: to pay the additional sum still owed.

допрежить.note: Wrong headword; the text word is the adverb/preposition допрежь (earlier, before), colloquial/archaic, as in 'допрежь того' = 'before that'.

допрезать.note: Wrong headword; the text word is допрежь, colloquial/archaic adverb 'before, previously'.

допросчик.note: Rare; the one conducting a допрос (interrogation).

дорезать.note: Perfective; here 'не дорезала' = did not finish the job of cutting (killing).

дорогонек.note: Colloquial diminutive-like form of дорогой; дорогонько is the adverb 'rather dearly'.

доселевый.note: Wrong headword; the text word is доселева, an archaic/colloquial adverb meaning 'until now'.

g: to ride at a gallop to
доскакать.note: Perfective; here 'Доскакали до...' = they galloped all the way to.

доставление.note: Verbal noun of доставить; 'для доставления себе удовольствия' = to give oneself pleasure.

доставша.note: Church Slavonic; 'не доставшу вину' = 'when the wine ran out' (John 2:3, dative absolute).

достоять.note: Church Slavonic form: 'не достоит' = 'it is not fitting/proper'.

g: to succeed in getting a response by knocking
достучаться.note: Perfective; достучаться = knock long enough to be let in.

досуха-с.note: досуха with servile particle -с (Smerdyakov's obsequious speech); 'тереть досуха' = rub until dry.

доткнентный.note: Polish, not Russian: 'Jestem do żywego dotknięty' = 'I am cut to the quick'; the text has a Polish phrase in Russian spelling.

дочка-мужичка.note: Compound; here мужичка is a feminine form of мужик (peasant) used as a modifier: a daughter who is a peasant woman.

дочка-мужичок.note: Wrong headword; the text has дочка-мужичка, with мужичка as feminine of мужик (peasant).

древлема.note: Wrong headword; the text form древлему is dative of древлий (Church Slavonic/archaic 'ancient'): 'по древлему обряду' = by the ancient rite.

дробинка.note: Single grain of shot (birdshot), diminutive of дробь; here loaded into a toy cannon.

друга.note: Wrong headword; text form is други, archaic/Church Slavonic plural of друг (friend), used as a form of address: 'Други мои' = my friends.

дурачество.note: From дурачиться (to play the fool); 'простить дурачеству' = forgive the foolery.

дурачье.note: Colloquial collective noun from дурак; dismissive/abusive.

дурища.note: Augmentative/pejorative of дура (fool, feminine); colloquial, here half-affectionate.

дуэльный.note: Here in the genitive plural: дуэльных пистолетов = duelling pistols.

дышать-дышать.note: Wrong headword: the text has the doubled form дышит-дышит, from дышать 'to breathe'; the repetition is for emphasis (breathes and breathes).

дышит-дышать.note: Wrong headword: the text has the doubled form дышит-дышит, from дышать; repetition conveys labored, continuous breathing.

дюжинк.note: Wrong headword: the form дюжинки is from the diminutive дюжинка, from дюжина 'dozen'.

дюжинка.note: Colloquial diminutive of дюжина; here in the genitive: три дюжинки = three dozen.

еврей-часовщик.note: Compound of еврей 'Jew' and часовщик 'watchmaker'; here in the dative: еврею-часовщику.

еврею-часовщик.note: Wrong headword: this is the dative of the compound еврей-часовщик.

европеизм.note: Here in the dative; the word appears in quotation marks in the text, referring to the Europeanized outlook of Ivan.

един.note: Church Slavonic/archaic form of один; едину is the accusative feminine, 'a single (minute)'.

едина.note: Church Slavonic/archaic feminine of един ('one'); едину is the accusative feminine, used emphatically: минуточку едину = one single minute.

единиться.note: Rare/bookish, related to единый; here 'the world grows ever more united'.

g: penitential discipline imposed by the Church
епитимия.note: Modern spelling епитимья; here in the plural: как епитимии = as acts of penance.

естем.note: Polish 'jestem' (I am), written in Russian letters as spoken by the Polish characters; e.g. естем готув = jestem gotów, 'I am ready'.

естема.note: Wrong headword: the form is Polish 'jestem' (I am), transliterated into Cyrillic as spoken by the Polish characters.

естественник.note: Dated term for someone who studied natural science; here instrumental: кончил курс естественником.

жалеючи.note: Dialectal/colloquial gerund of жалеть, used by the servant Smerdyakov; standard form is жалея.

жалеючий.note: Wrong headword: the text form жалеючи is a colloquial gerund of жалеть (standard жалея), not an adjective.

жалеючить.note: Wrong headword: the text form жалеючи is a colloquial gerund of жалеть (standard жалея).

жартовать.note: Polish 'żartować' (to joke), spoken by a Polish character; the text glosses it as 'шутишь'.

жартуесть.note: Wrong headword: the form is Polish 'żartujesz' (you're joking), from żartować, written in Cyrillic.

желаться.note: Impersonal use: желается = one wants/it is wished; here 'what he himself wants'.

желторотость.note: From желторотый ('yellow-beaked' = callow, naive); refers to youthful inexperience.

женимнуться.note: Wrong headword: женимшись is a nonstandard/dialectal gerund of жениться (standard женившись), in Smerdyakov's speech.

женимшиться.note: Wrong headword: женимшись is a nonstandard/dialectal gerund of жениться (standard женившись), in Smerdyakov's speech.

женный.note: Wrong headword: жено is the Church Slavonic vocative of жена ('woman, wife'), as in 'Woman, what have I to do with thee' (John 2:4).

женщина-соперница.note: Compound; here in the genitive plural: женщины-соперницы.

женщины-соперница.note: Wrong headword: the text form is the plural of the compound женщина-соперница.

женый.note: Wrong headword: жено is the Church Slavonic vocative of жена ('woman, wife').

жеребеночек.note: Diminutive of жеребёнок (foal); spelled жеребеночек without ё.

жестокосердный.note: Here as the adverb жестокосердно: 'cruelly, mercilessly'; a bookish/emphatic word.

живий.note: Polish-style/Ukrainian-like form; 'до живего' is Polish 'do żywego' meaning 'to the quick'. Spoken by a Polish character (естем до живего доткнентным = I am stung to the quick).

живодерность.note: Rare coinage from живодёр (flayer, tormentor); refers to merciless, exploitative nature.

жидененок.note: Derogatory/contemptuous diminutive from жид; here plural instrumental жиденятами, in the narrator's ironic listing of Jewish acquaintances.

жидишка.note: Derogatory diminutive of жид, offensive today; here instrumental plural жидишками.

жидишко.note: Derogatory diminutive of жид (Jew), offensive today; here genitive singular жидишки, in Rakitin's cynical speech.

жидовка.note: Derogatory term (жид is offensive in modern Russian); here instrumental, about Grushenka's business acumen: 'a regular Jewess'.

жизние.note: Wrong headword: жизнию is an archaic/bookish instrumental of жизнь ('life'), i.e. 'by life'.

жилочка.note: Diminutive of жила (vein, sinew); here plural instrumental жилочками, describing veined streaks in a stone.

жирненький.note: diminutive of жирный; here in the prepositional form 'на жирненьком личике' (a plump little face)

забеглый.note: colloquial; here of a dog that ran in from a village and settled

завиствовать.note: rare/dialectal; here a participle form, 'envious ones'; likely from завидовать

завиствующий.note: rare/dialectal participle of завиствовать; from завидовать; иных завиствующих = 'some of the envious'

завить.note: here завитой is a participle: with curled hair

завиться.note: in this context colloquial: 'пошёл, завился' means went off carousing

загноиться.note: used figuratively here: the people have 'festered' from drunkenness

загорланить.note: colloquial, perfective of горланить; here in the future tense: will start bawling a song

задирчивый.note: colloquial; related to задирать; the analyzer form given is the adverb задирчиво

задохся.note: masculine past tense of задохнуться; the headword form is nonstandard, the correct infinitive is задохнуться

задразнить.note: perfective of дразнить, with a sense of teasing someone to the limit

заживить.note: transitive; here figuratively 'заживить царапину' = to heal a scratch

заздравный.note: заздравный бокал = a glass raised in a toast to someone's health; from здравие

зазнамо.note: dated/colloquial; here in the phrase 'заранее и зазнамо' = beforehand and knowingly

зазорно.note: here used predicatively (short form): 'it was improper'; related to зазор (shame)

зазорный.note: dated; short forms зазорно, зазорен = shameful or improper

заискать.note: rare/dated; here 'искусство заискать' = the art of ingratiating oneself

g: to vow never to do again

заключиться.note: reflexive of заключить; in this text: 'to be completed' or 'to consist of'

g: to swear by all that is holy
заклясться-забожиться.note: colloquial doubled verb formed from заклясться + забожиться (to swear by God); the text has the form заклялась-забожилась

заколоться.note: reflexive of заколоть; закололся = stabbed himself

закопошиться.note: figurative here: jealousy began stirring again in his heart

закорузлой.note: form of закорузлый (callused, stiffened from wear/dirt); text has закорузлые sapozhki

закорузлый.note: of worn boots or hands; the text has the plural form закорузлые

закоулочек.note: diminutive of закоулок (back alley, blind alley)

закочевать.note: the participle закочевавший = who had wandered in (about the gypsy camp)

g: to cross with the sign of the cross
to make the sign of the cross over
закрестить.note: colloquial; закрестил = crossed him (to ward off a devil)

закурчавленный.note: participle of закурчавить/закурчавлить (to curl); of hair, like a ram's

закурчавлить.note: rare; the standard form is закурчавить; text has passive participle закурчавленные

закутить.note: Perfective; colloquial, often 'to start a binge'.

залавок.note: Dialectal/dated; a wooden bench or counter in a peasant hut; the text form залавке is prepositional.

заласкать.note: Colloquial; here ironic: 'how have you so charmed him?'

заливчатый.note: Describes ringing, rolling sounds such as laughter or sobbing.

залихватский.note: Colloquial; describes daring, lively songs or dances.

замечаньице.note: Diminutive of замечание, colloquial spelling замечаньице.

замолить.note: Here: 'mother prayed for me' (замолила about/за него).

замутиться.note: Here figurative: the Orthodox faith has become corrupted/blurred.

заплатать.note: Form заплатанном is participle 'patched'; standard is заплатанный.

заплатка.note: Nom. sg. заплатка, instr. pl. заплатками.

заплеснесть.note: Nonstandard variant; correct verb is заплесневеть.

запоить.note: Here: he plied peasants with champagne.

запредчувствовать.note: Rare; text form запредчувствовав is a gerund.

запрошлый.note: Colloquial; запрошлый год = year before last; here 'the generation before the last'.

запрячь-оседлать.note: Compound of запрячь and оседлать; text form запрягли-оседлали, used figuratively 'we've worked her like a horse'.

запылать.note: Perfective inchoative; figurative: burned with vengeance, cheeks flushed.

зарана.note: Dialectal/colloquial; text form заране; standard заранее.

заранний.note: Analyzer headword wrong; зараньше is a colloquial variant of the adverb заранее/заране.

зарез.note: Used in idiom до зарезу 'desperately, absolutely (need)'; text form зарезу.

g: to get carried away by one's act
зарисоваться.note: Colloquial; play-acting so much one half-believes it.

зарумяниться.note: Text form зарумянившись is a gerund.

зарябить.note: В глазах зарябило = things blurred before one's eyes.

g: to harden (from dirt or dried blood)
заскорузнуть.note: Colloquial; text form заскоруз is masculine past.

заскрежетать.note: Here: he ground out the words (as if gnashing teeth).

заслышаться.note: Rare/literary; impersonal, 'a note of sincerity could be heard'.

g: to make dirty with blowing nose
засморкать.note: Colloquial; text form засморканным is participle 'snot-stained'.

застегивание.note: Verbal noun of застёгивать; text form застегиванием is instrumental.

застегнуться.note: perfective, reflexive; here about fastening the borrowed clothes

затаскать.note: the text form затасканном is a past passive participle: worn-out, shabby

затмиться.note: солнце затмилось = the sun went dim, clouded over

затравка.note: small hole in a toy cannon where the powder is lit; 'затравку' is accusative

заучивание.note: verbal noun of заучивать; до заучивания наизусть = to the point of memorizing

заходятить.note: analyzer's headword is wrong; 'заходящу' is Church Slavonic dative of the participle заходящий (setting), see заходящ

заходящ.note: Church Slavonic participle; заходящу солнцу = 'to the setting sun' (dative, from Paschal-style phrasing, 'Christ conquered...')

захожий.note: used like a noun/adjective: a monk visiting from another monastery

захоца.note: not a lemma; form of захочу in peasant dialect/mock-rustic speech (захоцу = захочу); the refrain plays on вскочу 'I'll jump up'

захрустеть.note: perfective, inchoative; here about banknotes crackling like new

g: to appear as a dark mass
зачернеться.note: analyzer headword is off; the usual infinitive is зачернеться/зачернеть; here 'came into view as black'

зашибаться.note: colloquial; зашибать/зашибаться = drink hard; here in the infinitive used as a fragment

заштатный.note: historical: of clergy without an established position; заштатного дьякона = a deacon without a parish post

заштопать.note: заштопанное is a past passive participle: darned, mended

здзивеный.note: Polish (zdziwiony), rendered in Cyrillic; 'здзивёны' is a Polish speaker's form with 'быlem' = I was

здоровие.note: archaic/Church Slavonic form of здоровье; здоровии = prepositional case

здрова.note: Polish-influenced short form; бывай здрова = 'farewell, keep well' (Polish speaker's speech)

здровый.note: Polish-style form (zdrowy) of здоровый; здрова is feminine short form in 'farewell, be well'

зелие.note: Church Slavonic; in monastic fast rules зелие не варено = uncooked vegetables

земно.note: земно просит = humbly begs (from земной поклон, bowing to the ground); archaic

зиждать.note: Church Slavonic; зиждущие = 'the builders' (biblical: the stone the builders rejected)

зиждущее.note: participial form of зиждать, Church Slavonic; here plural 'зиждущие' = the builders

зиждущий.note: present active participle of зиждать; used as a noun: builders (Psalm 118:22 quotation)

зипунишка.note: derogatory diminutive of зипун, a coarse peasant coat; в зипунишке = prepositional

зипунишко.note: derogatory diminutive of зипун (neuter variant of зипунишка)

златокудрый.note: poetic/archaic; златокудрый Феб = golden-haired Phoebus (Apollo, the sun)

злословник.note: rare/archaic derivative of злословие; злословников is genitive plural

злото.note: Polish: złoto / złoty; in the Polish card-game dialogue, a stake in money

злющая-презлоть.note: wrong headword; the text has the folk-tale phrase злющая-презлющая (злющий + intensifying пре-)

злющая-презлющий.note: folk-tale repetition злющая-презлющая = very, very mean; from злющий with intensifier пре-

злющий.note: colloquial intensive of злой; злющая, злющего, злющие = inflected forms

злющий-презлющий.note: Intensive reduplication of злющий (very wicked, from злой) with the prefix пре-; folk-tale style, as in the onion parable.

знамо.note: Colloquial/dialectal; short for 'знамо дело' (of course, naturally).

знамша.note: Servant Smerdyakov's nonstandard speech form; correct standard participle is зная. Analyzer headword is wrong; the form is знамши (from знать).

знамшить.note: Not a real verb; знамши is a colloquial, uneducated gerund of знать (standard: зная). Smerdyakov's affected speech.

знахарский.note: From знахарь (folk healer, wise man); here 'знахарскому чуду' = a sorcerer's/folk-magic miracle.

знач.note: 'значи' is a Polish-accented/mangled form of значит (it means, so) in the mouth of a Polish character.

игривость.note: Genitive of игривость; here ironic: the frivolity of the doctor's conclusion.

игуменский.note: From игумен (abbot, hegumen); e.g. игуменская кухня = the abbot's kitchen; сан игуменский = the abbot's rank.

иезуитский.note: From иезуит (Jesuit); often figurative: sophistical, crafty.

иеродиакон.note: Eastern Orthodox monk who is also a deacon; here dative plural иеродиаконам.

иеросхимонах.note: Orthodox monk-priest of the highest monastic rank (great schema); Elder Zosima's rank.

избимшить.note: Not a real verb; избимши is Smerdyakov's nonstandard gerund of избить (standard: избив).

изверг-отцеубивец.note: Compound of изверг (monster, fiend) and отцеубийца (parricide; the variant отцеубивец is archaic/rhetorical).

извещаться.note: Impersonal past 'извещалось' = it was reported (in the press); passive/reflexive of извещать.

извинительный.note: Here in short neuter form/adverbial use: 'извинительно' = it is excusable.

извозчичий.note: From извозчик (cab driver); here 'извозчичья коляска' = a hired carriage.

издохнуть.note: Coarse when applied to people; here 'I'll die like a dog there'.

излечиться.note: Perfective; 'излечиться от любви к человечеству' = to be cured of love for humanity.

изменница.note: Feminine of изменник; instrumental case 'изменницей'; here Grushenka seen as faithless.

изможечь.note: Analyzer headword is wrong; the form belongs to изможденный/изможжённый (worn out), participle of изможить/изнурить.

изможженный.note: Dostoevsky's spelling of standard изможденный (with -жд- replaced by -жж-).

изможжить.note: Rare/dialectal variant of standard изможденный/изнурить; изможженным is a participle form.

износиться.note: Here figurative: 'words have all worn out (become trite)'.

изразцовый.note: From изразец (glazed decorative tile); 'изразцовая печь' = tiled stove.

изъяснение.note: Bookish; 'изъяснение в любви' = a declaration of love.

изыда.note: Church Slavonic: изыти/изыду = I will go out; 'изыди' also = 'begone!'. Analyzer headword is wrong; form is изыду (1st person future).

изыдесть.note: Wrong headword; form 'изыдешь' = you will go out, from Church Slavonic изыти.

изысть.note: Wrong headword; form 'изыдешь' is 2nd person future of Church Slavonic изыти (go forth), correct lemma изыти.

изыхать.note: Wrong headword; 'изыдешь' comes from Church Slavonic изыти (go forth).

имемша.note: Smerdyakov's nonstandard gerund form; the actual form is имемши (from иметь, standard: имев). Analyzer headword is wrong.

имемшить.note: Not a real verb; имемши is Smerdyakov's nonstandard gerund of иметь ('никаких сведений не имемши' = having no information).

именование.note: Bookish; 'по прежнему именованию' = by its former name.

индюшечка.note: Diminutive of индюшка (turkey hen); playful in Fyodor Pavlovich's speech.

ино.note: Church Slavonic/archaic; in 'ино ласточкой, ино щеглом' = now as a swallow, now as a goldfinch; in the fasting rule = 'other'.

иносказательный.note: From иносказание (allegory); here 'в иносказательном смысле' = in a figurative sense.

иноческий.note: From инок (monk); 'иноческий подвиг' = monastic feat/ascetic labor.

иноязычник.note: Archaic/church usage: one of another tongue or faith, a non-Christian; here in Smerdyakov's argument about cursing God.

g: girl from a boarding institute for noble girls
институтка.note: Colloquial term for a pupil or graduate of a women's institute (Katerina Ivanovna).

инфернальница.note: Coined feminine noun from инфернальный; Mitya's term for a diabolical woman.

инфернальный.note: From French/Latin infernal; the forms in text include the adverb инфернально ('diabolically').

искательный.note: The text form искательно is the adverb.

искатить.note: Wrong headword; искати is Church Slavonic infinitive of искать ('to seek'), from Philippians 3:20 quoted in Slavonic.

искать-искать.note: Not a real headword; ищет-ищет is repetition of ищет (искать) for emphasis.

искривленно.note: Adverb of искривлённый; used of a face or smile.

искривленный.note: The text form искривленно is the adverb.

испити.note: Church Slavonic infinitive of испить; from the monastic fasting rule text.

исповедальный.note: Here used as a noun-like adjective: confessional booths.

исповедование.note: Verbal noun of исповедовать; here the ongoing confessing of one's soul to the elder.

исполнимый.note: Text form исполнимо is the short neuter/predicative form: 'it is feasible'.

исправничий.note: Possessive adjective from исправник; the 'police chief's daughters'.

испытовать.note: Wrong headword; испытуешь is the archaic/literary verb испытовать/испытывать form ('you test me').

испытуесть.note: Wrong headword; испытуешь is 2nd person of the archaic испытовать/испытывать.

испытующий.note: Present active participle of the literary verb испытовать; used of looks and smiles.

иссякновение.note: Bookish noun from иссякнуть; here: the loss of belief in immortality.

истереться.note: Form истершеюся is the feminine instrumental of the participle истёршийся ('worn out'), here with dialectal/old ending.

истерическа.note: Wrong headword; the form is the adverb истерически ('hysterically').

истязательный.note: The text form истязательно is the adverb.

истязовать.note: Rare/nonstandard headword; the standard verb is истязать, and истязуемой is its passive participle form.

истязуемый.note: Present passive participle of истязать (in the older form истязовать); often used as a noun ('the victim').

истязуть.note: Wrong headword; истязуемому is dative of the participle истязуемый from истязать/истязовать.

исцелесть.note: Wrong headword; исцелевшую is the participle of исцелеть ('to be healed, recover').

исцелеть.note: Rare perfective verb; исцелевшую is accusative feminine past active participle ('the healed (girl)').

исцелитель.note: Elevated/religious word, here addressed to the elder Zosima.

исьць.note: Polish (spelled in Russian letters) for iść, 'to go'; spoken by a Pole in the tavern scene, in the phrase 'if you want to go with me, let's go'.

ищет-искать.note: Not a real headword; ищет-ищет is reduplicated ищет (искать), for emphasis of repeated action.

к-крак.note: Onomatopoeia with a stutter/emphasis, imitating the sound of the goose's neck breaking.

к-крака.note: Wrong headword; the text form к-крак is an onomatopoeic interjection 'crack!'.

кадриль.note: A square dance of French origin; feminine noun.

каждогодный.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong; the text form is the adverb каждогодно (every year).

казенщина.note: Derogatory; something done in a stiff, impersonal, government-issue way.

казуист.note: Used as an insult: someone who twists arguments over fine points.

кантик.note: Diminutive of кант (edging); here the trimmed edge of a cap.

каплун.note: Figurative insult here: castrated cock, i.e. spineless people.

карамазовский.note: Coined from the surname Карамазов; denotes their sensual, unrestrained character.

карамазовщина.note: Coined with -щина (like обломовщина); pejorative for the family's disorder.

кардинальский.note: From кардинал (Catholic cardinal); refers to the Grand Inquisitor.

картинность.note: Here with a slightly negative sense of showy effect.

ква-ква.note: Onomatopoeia for a duck; from a nursery-style song.

квадриллионный.note: Here in the phrase 'to the quadrillionth power'; humorous hyperbole.

кипень.note: Found in the idiom 'белый как кипень' (snow-white).

кипучий.note: Here describes youthful energy and hot blood.

клака.note: In the text used loosely for a burst of applause from the audience.

клакер.note: Someone who applauds on cue; here the courtroom audience.

клерикал.note: Ironic quotation marks in the text; means the monastery party.

кликуша.note: Peasant women subject to shrieking fits believed to be demonic possession.

кликуша-то.note: Form of кликуша with emphatic particle -то; here refers to Alyosha's mother.

кляститься.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong; the text has клястись, i.e. клясться.

кнутик.note: Diminutive of кнут; here in the instrumental form кнутиком.

кнутиком.note: Instrumental of кнутик, diminutive of кнут (whip).

кнутикома.note: Wrong headword; the form is instrumental кнутиком of кнутик (little whip).

g: to clown, to act the buffoon
коверкаться.note: Here: to grimace and play the fool.

кодрант.note: From Biblical Church Slavonic (Matthew 5:26), from Latin quadrans; 'to the last farthing'.

кой-какой.note: Indefinite pronoun; here 'some bits of information'.

кой-что.note: Indefinite pronoun; inflected form кой-чему means 'a thing or two' as dative.

колбаснический.note: Contemptuous, from колбасник (German sausage-maker); implies narrow-minded, German-style servility.

коленкома.note: Wrong headword: the form is instrumental of коленко (colloquial for колено, knee); 'коленком напинать' = to kick with the knee.

коленок.note: Wrong headword: form is instrumental 'коленком' of коленко/колено, colloquial 'knee'.

колеска.note: Wrong headword: 'на колесках' is the prepositional plural of колесо or колёсико (small wheel), diminutive.

колесок.note: Wrong headword: 'на колесках' is diminutive plural of колесо (wheel), on little wheels.

коломянка.note: Cheap durable fabric used for summer clothes.

комедиант.note: Here figurative: a man who plays a part, a fraud.

комедь.note: Colloquial/archaic form of комедия; 'комедь играть' = to put on an act.

компаньишко.note: Contemptuous diminutive of компания/компанья in the speaker's mocking style.

контроверза.note: Archaic loanword (Latin controversia); here a chapter title, Book XII chapter.

конфеточка.note: Diminutive of конфета; 'конфеточек' is genitive plural.

конфузный.note: 'Конфузно' is predicative/adverbial: 'it is embarrassing'; from конфузить (to embarrass).

концентричный.note: Dostoevsky uses adverb концентрично to mean concentrated, focused, in relief.

корпия.note: Old medical term: shredded linen used as wound dressing.

котиковый.note: From котик (fur seal); котиковая фуражка = sealskin cap.

который-нибудь.note: Indefinite: 'за которую-нибудь' = over some woman or other.

кр-р-р.note: Onomatopoeia of crunching; here stretched with extra р in 'кр-р-рах'; the word is actually 'крах' (crack).

крепостник.note: Used as a political insult in the reform era.

крепостничий.note: Standard form is крепостнический; крепостничье отродье = 'serf-owner brood'.

g: dear blood (my own flesh and blood)

крошечка.note: Diminutive of крошка; 'ни крошечки' = not a bit.

крулев.note: Wrong headword: 'крулева' is a Polish-flavored form of королева (queen), spoken by the Poles.

крулевый.note: Wrong headword: 'крулева' = Polish królowa 'queen', see королева.

ктур.note: Wrong headword: foreign, Polish 'Która godzina, panie?' = 'What time is it, sir?'; spelled Russian-style.

кубарь.note: Colloquial; кубари спускать = to spin tops.

кулачат.note: Form of кулачить/кулачить: to act as a kulak, profiteer and dominate the market.

кулачонка.note: Wrong headword: 'кулачонками' is instrumental plural of кулачонок, diminutive of кулак (fist).

кулачонкий.note: Wrong headword: 'кулачонком' is instrumental of кулачонок, diminutive of кулак.

куметь.note: Wrong headword: 'Талифа куми' is Aramaic (Mark 5:41) 'Talitha cumi', 'little girl, arise'; quoted in Church Slavonic.

купчик.note: diminutive of купец; often slightly mocking; the second quote is a folk-song line

купчина.note: augmentative of купец; colloquial, slightly disparaging

g: small pouch worn on the neck
ладонка.note: nonstandard spelling of ладанка (bag with incense/relics worn on the chest)

g: small pouch worn on the neck
ладонкий.note: wrong headword; the form ладонкой is instrumental of ладонка (= ладанка)

лазеть-с.note: servile -с particle; form лазею-с is Smerdyakov's nonstandard 1st person of лазить (лажу)

лайдак.note: Polish łajdak; said by the Poles in the scene

лакомствовать.note: dated; used ironically by Dmitri and Ракитин

лаптишка.note: diminutive/pejorative of лапоть; лаптишках is prepositional plural

легконогий.note: here a jesting euphemism for a promiscuous woman

лжеподобие.note: rare, book-style; here a false image of Christ

ликерец.note: diminutive of ликёр; ликерцем is instrumental, ликерцу partitive genitive

лисить.note: colloquial; from лиса (fox); more common: лебезить/лисить

лихоимствовать.note: archaic/biblical; imperative лихоимствуйте with negation 'Do not extort'

лишимнуться.note: nonstandard spelling of лишиться; the lemma is a mistaken guess

лишимшиться.note: Smerdyakov's nonstandard participle лишимшись for лишившись (from лишиться)

ложесна.note: Church Slavonic plural (ложесна); biblical, from Luke 'the womb'; Smerdyakov quotes it mockingly

ложесный.note: wrong headword; ложесна is Church Slavonic plural of ложесно (womb)

ложесон.note: wrong headword; ложесна is Church Slavonic plural for 'womb'

лучиночки.note: wrong headword form; correct lemma is лучиночка (diminutive of лучина)

лучиночко.note: Wrong headword; correct lemma is лучиночка, diminutive of лучина (splinter, sliver).

людье.note: Archaic/Church Slavonic plural 'людие' (= люди), from a holy man's speech.

лютеранствуть.note: Wrong headword; the participle лютеранствующий comes from the verb лютеранствовать.

лютеранствующий.note: Participle of лютеранствовать; used ironically of Russians imitating Protestant piety.

ляд.note: Colloquial, euphemism for чёрт; 'на кой ляд' = 'what the devil for'.

ляд-с.note: 'ляд' with the servile particle -с (from сударь), as spoken by Smerdyakov.

мазурик.note: Colloquial; from the old sense of a pickpocket or petty thief.

маленький-маленький.note: Doubled adjective for emphasis; text has the accusative feminine form маленькую-маленькую.

маленькую-маленький.note: Wrong headword; it is the accusative feminine of маленький-маленький (tiny), doubled for emphasis.

маловерный.note: Biblical/Church Slavonic flavor ('O ye of little faith'); also used as a noun.

малоречивый.note: Bookish; text has short form малоречив.

малосильный.note: Literally 'of little strength'; here of the weak human mind.

малословный.note: Rare; here describes a short, wordless farewell.

малыий.note: Smerdyakov's deliberately odd/mock-folksy form of 'с малым'; the narrator then asks why not just say 'с малым'.

мальц-экстракт.note: From German Malzextrakt; the Hoff brand malt extract was a popular tonic in 19th-century Russia.

мальчик-левша.note: Compound noun; the accusative is мальчика-левшу.

мальчика-левша.note: Wrong headword; correct is мальчик-левша (accusative мальчика-левшу).

маменька.note: Affectionate, somewhat old-fashioned diminutive of мать.

маменька-то.note: Form of маменька with the emphatic particle -то.

мамзель.note: Colloquial Russification of French mademoiselle, often slightly ironic.

мамуровка.note: Colloquial/dialectal; a kind of homemade sweet liqueur or cordial.

манишка.note: Detachable shirt front worn under a jacket or vest.

мараться.note: Often figurative: to sully oneself by getting involved.

математически.note: Here: with absolute clarity or exactness.

математичность.note: Noun from математический; refers to Mitya's reputation for punctilious exactness.

матерью-земля.note: Wrong headword; correct is мать-земля, here in the instrumental (матерью-землёю).

маточка.note: Colloquial/folk endearment; here a term of affection addressed to a woman.

мгновеньице.note: Diminutive of мгновение (moment), used for ironic effect.

меблированный.note: Participial adjective from меблировать; here a room furnished with old furniture.

меблировать.note: The text has the participle меблированный (furnished).

g: Medelyansky (of a large breed of hunting dog)
меделянский.note: Refers to an old Russian breed of large dog (mastiff type) named after Milan; 'меделянский щенок' = puppy of that breed.

мейсец.note: Polish 'miejsce'; from the Polish characters' speech ('На мейсца!' = to your places!).

мелко-надменный.note: Compound of мелкий and надменный, describing a petty, proud soul.

мелкоподрядный.note: From мелкий подряд (small contract); here 'a small contracting business'.

меняльный.note: Dated adjective from меняла (money changer); меняльная лавка = money-changing shop.

мериться.note: Passive in the biblical proverb (мерится = is measured out); reflexive 'measure oneself (one's height)' in the second sentence.

мефистофелевский.note: From Mephistopheles (Goethe's Faust). Neuter form мефистофелевское.

мець.note: Polish (mieć), spoken by the Polish characters; not Russian.

мигрений.note: Wrong headword; the text form мигреня is a nonstandard genitive of мигрень (migraine).

мигренить.note: Wrong headword; the word in the text is мигреня, a form of мигрень 'migraine'.

мигреня.note: Colloquial/old form of мигрень; here genitive ('an attack of migraine').

милосердый.note: Archaic/Church Slavonic-flavored variant of милосердный; милосерд is the short form.

мимоидущий.note: Church Slavonic-style participle; modern мимо идущий/преходящий.

минуться.note: Archaic/poetic; standard form is пройти/минуть; минется = will pass.

g: rich peasant who preys on the commune
мироед.note: Pejorative for a kulak-type who bleeds the peasant community (мир).

миусовский.note: Possessive adjective from the surname Миусов; here dative masculine миусовскому (nephew).

младенческа.note: Wrong headword; the form in the text is младенчески, adverb from младенческий (infantile, childlike).

многолетный.note: The text form многолетно is used adverbially ('over many years', persistently); the adjective is многолетний.

многоречивый.note: Bookish; многоречив is the short form.

многоречий.note: Wrong headword; the text has многоречию, dative of многоречие (verbosity).

многочтить.note: Wrong headword; the text has многочтимой, from the adjective/participle многочтимый 'highly esteemed', ironically paired with многоуважаемый.

моген.note: Polish-flavored/mock speech of the Poles (Polish mogę / Russian могу); 'Чем моген служиць' = 'how can I serve'.

могий.note: Wrong headword; могим is a peasant/nonstandard form of the verb (мы) можем: 'we can judge'.

можа.note: Polish-style (może) in the mouth of a Pole; not Russian.

мокретить.note: Wrong headword; the text has мокреть, a colloquial noun meaning wet, damp, rainy weather.

мокринский.note: Adjective from the village name Мокрое (Mokroye).

молебщик.note: From молебен; a person who offers prayers on behalf of others.

молельщик.note: Variant of молебщик; someone praying for another.

моление.note: Church Slavonic-flavored; 'нежный до моления' = tender to the point of supplication.

g: to act younger than one's age
молодиться.note: Text has the participle молодящаяся 'trying to look young'.

молодцеватый.note: молодцевато is the adverb ('jauntily, with bravado').

молчальник.note: Used of monks who keep silence as an ascetic practice.

молчальный.note: Rare adjective from молчать; here feminine молчальная (улыбочка).

монпансье.note: Indeclinable; from French monpensier, a kind of boiled sweets sold in tins.

монструозный.note: Here the adverb form монструозно ('it's outrageous'); a bookish borrowing from Latin/French monstrueux.

моор.note: Surname of Karl Moor, the hero of Schiller's play 'The Robbers' (Die Räuber); a proper name, not a common word.

моравский.note: «Моравские братья» = the Moravian Brethren (Herrnhuter), a pietist Protestant sect.

мордасы.note: Colloquial/humorous plural noun (usually мордасы); 'по мордасам' = 'across the face', i.e. slap or thrash. From морда.

му-му.note: Onomatopoeia for a cow's lowing, from a children's-style song.

мувена.note: Wrong headword. In text 'мувен' is Polish mówię, 'I speak/say', transliterated; 'ниц не мувен' = 'I said nothing'. Speech of Polish characters.

мувено.note: Wrong headword. 'мувен' is Polish mówię ('I say'), in the phrase 'ниц не мувен против' = 'I said nothing against'.

муви.note: Polish mówi ('he/she says'), transliterated in the speech of Polish characters.

мувить.note: Polish mówić, transliterated; 'цо мувишь' = 'what you say', from the Polish proverb 'co mówisz, to się stanie'.

мувиць.note: Polish mówić (to speak), in Polish-flavored speech; 'так мувиць не пржистои' = 'it is not proper to speak so'.

мувный.note: Wrong headword. 'мувен' is Polish mówię ('I say'); a transliterated Polish word in the Poles' speech.

мужичий.note: Derived from мужик (peasant); slightly dismissive or colloquial.

мужичонкий.note: Wrong headword; the correct one is мужичонко (or мужичонка), a contemptuous or pitying diminutive of мужик.

мужичонко.note: Diminutive-pejorative of мужик (peasant), with a pitying or contemptuous tone.

мучающийся.note: Present active participle of мучаться (to suffer); dative case мучающемуся.

мучительски.note: Colloquial/nonstandard adverb from мучитель; 'мучительски мучить' = 'to torment mercilessly'.

мыслибус.note: Humorous fake-Latin form of мысль, from the tag 'de gustibus non est disputandum' (there is no arguing about tastes), twisted to 'de мыслибус'.

мыслибусы.note: Wrong headword; 'мыслибус' is a mock-Latin ending on мысль, parodying 'de gustibus non est disputandum'.

мыслие.note: Archaic/bookish form of мысль; 'этою мыслию' is instrumental singular (modern мыслью).

мястись.note: Wrong headword; the correct one is мятущийся (from метаться/мятись), 'restless, agitated, tormented'. The form 'мятущегося' is the genitive of the participle-adjective.

н-нет-с.note: Hesitant 'нет' with the servile particle -с (from сударь), a stammered polite refusal.

наафонить.note: Slang, from офеня/афоня (peddler cant); 'наафонил я' = 'I've conned my share'; slangy colloquial.

наблюсти.note: Bookish; here 'to see to, keep watch over', i.e. to uphold one's own dignity.

навыдумать.note: Perfective of навыдумывать, colloquial; 'навыдумала себе препятствия' = 'dreamed up obstacles'.

навыдумывать.note: Colloquial; 'навыдумывал ужасов' = 'imagined all kinds of horrors'.

нагло-вызывать.note: Wrong headword; 'нагло-вызывающее' is a compound adjective form of нагло-вызывающий, 'brazenly challenging'.

нагло-вызывающий.note: Compound of нагло (insolently) + вызывающий (challenging); neuter form here.

наглупить.note: Colloquial perfective, from глупить (to act stupidly).

наглядело.note: Wrong headword; 'наглядел' is past masculine of наглядеть, 'to spot, pick out'.

наглядеть.note: Colloquial; 'давно наглядел' = 'had long had my eye on'.

нагорать.note: Said of a candle whose wick chars and grows long ('свечка нагорала').

g: to blurt out a heap of nonsense
нагородить.note: Colloquial; 'нагородить ахинеи' = 'to talk a load of rubbish'.

наготовить.note: Perfective; here the passive participle-like 'наготовлено' = 'has been prepared'.

наградной.note: 'Наградные (деньги)' = reward money, tip or bonus; here genitive plural used as a noun.

наградные.note: Plural noun (from наградные деньги), a bonus or fee given as a reward.

нагреметь.note: Colloquial perfective of греметь (to thunder, clatter); 'нашумит, нагремит' = 'makes a lot of noise'.

g: to add to a price or offer

надворный.note: надворные строения = outbuildings; надворный советник = Court Councillor, a rank in the Table of Ranks

надзвездный.note: here spelled надзвездную; ironic in Ivan's speech

надотить.note: analyzer error; the text form is the dialectal predicate надоть, see надоть

надоть.note: dialectal/colloquial for надо; 'надоть быть' = 'probably, must be' in peasant speech

надрезать.note: надрезано is the short passive participle: slit, notched (ear)

надсмехаться.note: colloquial variant of насмехаться, used with над + instrumental

надтреснутый.note: надтреснутым голосом = in a cracked voice

надуматься.note: perfective; here 'as if he had made up his mind'

назидательный.note: form назидательно is the adverb; the lemma is the adjective

наистрожайше.note: superlative with наи- of строжайше; emphatic, somewhat archaic

наистрожайший.note: text form наистрожайше is the adverb; наи- is an archaic superlative prefix

найлепнуть.note: wrong headword; найлепши is Polish 'najlepszy', 'the best', spoken by the Poles

наказовать.note: archaic/Church Slavonic form of наказывать; наказую = 'I punish', наказуй = 'punish!'

наказуй.note: archaic imperative of наказовать/наказывать; the text also has наказую 'I punish'

наказый.note: wrong headword; наказую is the archaic 1st person of наказовать, 'to punish'

накашиваться.note: here 'на лужайке накашивалось' = several poods of hay were mown each summer

наколотить.note: here colloquial: 'наколотишь рубль на копейку' = you'll make a rouble on a kopeck

наколочка.note: diminutive of наколка, a lady's ornamental headpiece

накутиль.note: analyzer error; correct infinitive is накутить, colloquial 'to make a spree, cause a rumpus'

накутить.note: colloquial; 'что мы там накутили' = what a fuss we made there

налево-то-с.note: налево + emphatic -то + servile particle -с (from сударь), typical of Smerdyakov's speech

наперерыв.note: often наперебой/наперегонки sense; 'все наперерыв' = everyone vying

написаться.note: perfective reflexive; 'не написалось' = would not have got written

наплывной.note: rare; 'наплывным ветром' = by some drifting, passing wind

наполниша.note: Church Slavonic aorist 3rd pl. of наполнити (наполнить); from the Gospel of John (Cana wedding)

напомадить.note: напомаженный = pomaded, slicked with hair oil

напророчить.note: Perfective; here 'словно и напророчил' = 'as if he had prophesied it'.

напутственный.note: Used in 'напутственное слово' = parting words, words of send-off or final instruction.

наразбить.note: Nonstandard/dialectal; here the adverbial participle 'наразбив' means 'piecemeal, in a scattered way', citing facts out of order.

насадиться.note: Passive/reflexive of насадить; here said of the institution of elders (старчество) being established at the monastery.

наседка.note: Here 'к наседке' = to the mother hen, of chicks huddling to it.

насказать-с.note: Form 'насказали-с' with servile particle -с (Smerdyakov's obsequious speech). Perfective of насказать.

насмешник.note: Forms in text: насмешники, насмешникам, насмешников (plural).

g: to laugh at, make fun of
to have one's fill of laughing
насмеяться.note: 'Насмеешься' = you'll have your laugh (at someone's expense); 'насмеяться над' = to mock.

насмотреть.note: Colloquial perfective, 'давно насмотрел' = I've had my eye on her for a long time.

насоздаваль.note: Wrong headword; the correct lemma is насоздавать (perfective, 'to create a lot of').

насоздавать.note: Colloquial perfective; 'насоздавали романов' = have created (lots of) novels.

насоздать.note: Colloquial perfective, 'насоздаст себе новых чудес' = will create for himself new miracles.

наставиться.note: Here 'наставившись на Митю, как петухи' = squaring up to Mitya like roosters.

наустить.note: Colloquial; 'он меня наустил' = he put me up to it.

научение.note: Here 'без научения' = without being taught (genitive form научения).

g: to dye or wax (a moustache) black
нафабрить.note: From фабра (moustache dye/wax); 'нафабренные усики' = waxed, blackened little moustaches.

g: to act up, make a fuss
нафонзонить.note: Colloquial, apparently from the surname Фонвизин/'Фонзон'; here 'что ты там нафонзонил' = what have you been up to/causing there. Meaning is somewhat uncertain.

нахвататься.note: Colloquial; 'где вы этого нахватались' = where did you pick that up.

начальствовать.note: The form 'начальствующее' is really a participle of this verb ('the one in command').

начальствующий.note: Participle used as adjective; 'начальствующее лицо' = person in authority.

начетливость.note: Refers to being well-read in religious texts ('от божественного'); noun from начетливый.

нашалить.note: Perfective of шалить; forms нашалит (3sg), нашалят (3pl).

наэлектризовать.note: Figurative; 'наэлектризованы' = were electrified, keyed up (past passive participle).

небедный.note: Formed with не- + бедный; 'небедная вдова' = a comfortably-off widow.

небесеха.note: Wrong headword. 'на небесех' is Church Slavonic locative plural of небеса, from a Bible quotation (Phil. 3:20: 'our citizenship is in heaven').

небесить.note: Wrong headword. 'на небеси' is the Church Slavonic locative singular of небо/небеса ('in heaven'); archaic/biblical.

неблагородный.note: Not noble in character; forms: неблагородного, неблагородным.

неблизкий.note: Here the adverb 'неблизко' = not soon/far off in time or distance.

небрезгливый.note: Here of a plan that is coarse, showing no delicacy.

невежливость.note: Here in instrumental: 'с невежливостью' = with rudeness.

невероятность.note: Noun from невероятный; 'невероятность выдумки' = the implausibility of the fabrication.

невзирая.note: Gerund of невзирать; 'невзирая на' = regardless of; a somewhat bookish preposition-like use.

невмочь.note: Colloquial predicative; 'ему невмочь' = he can't stand/bear it.

невоздержный.note: Applied to a person who indulges without limits, especially in drink.

невыгода.note: Genitive невыгоды; here 'некоторой для себя невыгоды' = some disadvantage to himself.

невыдержка.note: Noun from невыдержанный; 'молодая невыдержка' = youthful lack of restraint.

невыясниться.note: Analyzer's headword is off; the form невыясниvшийся is a participle of невыясниться, meaning 'not yet clarified/defined'.

недодать.note: Here недоданное/недоданных is a past passive participle: 'not given in full, withheld'.

недружелюбный.note: Short form недружелюбен = 'was unfriendly'; недружелюбно is the adverb.

незавершиться.note: Here a participle: 'unfinished, incomplete (time/age)'; normally written as не завершившийся.

незаживать.note: Participle незаживавшая = 'unhealed, never-healing'; normally спelled не заживавшая.

незапятнать.note: Really the short adjective form незапятнано (from незапятнанный): 'unsullied, spotless'.

незначащий.note: Present participle of значить with не-; also normally written незначащий.

неизбежимый.note: Nonstandard/dialectal-sounding variant of неизбежный (or of неминуемый).

неизбежить.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong; the form неизбежимым is an adjective (see неизбежимый), a variant of неизбежный.

неизменимый.note: Here neuter short form неизменимо: 'it cannot be changed'.

неизменить.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong; неизменимо is the short adjective form of неизменимый.

неискаженный.note: Text spells adverb неискаженно without ё: 'in undistorted form'.

неискупленный.note: Here refers to tears not atoned for/avenged; also diminutive слезки in the text.

неисповедимый.note: Set phrase: неисповедимые судьбы (Providence's ways are inscrutable); church register.

нейти.note: Really не идут: negation не + идти (нейдут is a fused, older spelling).

некаторжный.note: Coined by contrast: 'one who is not a convict'; normally не каторжному.

некиий.note: Church Slavonic form; correct lemma is некий. Genitive plural некиих: 'certain (things)'.

нелегкомысленный.note: Normally written не легкомысленные; used of Grigory's weighty words.

нелюбопытный.note: In this usage means 'not interesting/boring', not 'incurious'.

неминучий.note: Dated/folk-flavored; here of the spasm that inevitably seized him (epileptic fit).

немудрено.note: Predicative use: немудрено, что... = 'it is no wonder that...'.

немудреный.note: Form немудрено is the predicative 'no wonder'; the analyzer's headword немудрёный means 'simple, unsophisticated'.

немудрый.note: In the text: 'простодушное немудрое веселие' = simple, artless joy.

ненасытимо.note: Adverb of ненасытимый; rare/literary, formed with the -им- suffix (cf. ненасытно).

ненасытить.note: Analyzer's headword is wrong; the forms come from the adjective ненасытимый (insatiable), not a verb.

необделанный.note: Literally 'not worked/finished'; here describes raw, unpolished force.

необширный.note: Short form необширна; negation of обширный (spacious).

неопределимый.note: Sometimes spelled неопределимый; the text has the feminine неопределимая.

неотвязный.note: The forms in text are the adverb неотвязно; the adjective describes something that won't leave one alone.

неотлучно.note: Adverb of неотлучный; from отлучиться 'to go away'.

неотлучный.note: The forms in text are the adverb неотлучно.

неотомщенный.note: Participial adjective from отомстить; ё not written in the text (неотомщенный).

неотразимость.note: Noun from неотразимый; here the irrefutable force of the accusation.

неповинный.note: Somewhat archaic/literary; cf. невиновный. Short form неповинен.

неподвластный.note: Here substantivized in the genitive plural: those not under authority.

непочтительно.note: Adverb of непочтительный; also used predicatively ('it was disrespectful').

непреоборимый.note: Literary variant of непреодолимый/непобедимый; from преоборить 'to overcome'.

неприютный.note: Quoted here from Schiller-style poetry; describes shores offering no shelter.

непропорциональный.note: Here: strikingly unequal in height compared to the other man.

непщовать.note: Archaic Church Slavonic word; Непщуйте is the imperative 'think/judge for yourselves'.

неразрешенный.note: Participial adjective from разрешить; ё not written in the text.

нераспечатанный.note: Here of a fresh deck of cards; from распечатать 'to unseal'.
